title: Rectangular beam
spec: To construct a rectangular beam, start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and a translation vector of zero, zero, and zero. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face, which consists of a single loop made up of four straight lines. The first line starts at the origin and ends at coordinates zero point one zero two three, zero. The second line extends from this point to zero point one zero two three, zero point zero five eight. The third line moves back to zero, zero point zero five eight, and the fourth line completes the loop by returning to the origin. After drawing the sketch, apply a scaling factor of zero point one zero two three to ensure the dimensions are accurate. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into three dimensions by rotating it using the same Euler angles and translating it with the same vector. Finally, extrude the sketch zero point seven five units along the normal direction to create a new solid body. This results in a rectangular beam with a flat top and bottom, square edges, and a consistent cross-section. The beam has a length of zero point one zero two two seven two seven two seven two seven two seven, a width of zero point zero five seven nine five four five four five four five four five, and a height of zero point seven five units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.1023, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.1023, 0.058) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.058) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
# The translation vector is [0, 0, 0], so no translation is needed
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# Final model
print(r)

     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.1023) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.1023) \
